339514.title: The switch map's dinv and fixed-point conjecture
339514.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_{3,n}$ be the set of $(3,n)$-parking functions, let $\operatorname{pides}(\pi)=2^a1^b$, let $\Phi$ be the involution whose fixed points are the fixed parking functions, and let $\mathbb{S}$ be the switch map. **The switch-map conjecture.** For any $\pi\in\mathcal{P}_{3,n}$ with $\operatorname{pides}(\pi)=2^a1^b$, (a) 
$$
\operatorname{dinv}(\pi)=\operatorname{dinv}(\mathbb{S}(\pi)).
$$
 (b) When $n$ and $3$ are coprime, if $\pi$ is a fixed point of $\Phi$, then so is $\mathbb{S}(\pi)$, and 
$$
\operatorname{pides}(\mathbb{S}(\pi))=2^b1^a.
$$
 The conjecture was verified for parking functions with at most 10 rows, while the text notes that part (b) fails when $n$ is a multiple of $3$.
339514.review_depth: Source §2.1 Definitions 2–9 and §5.2.2 map, Theorems 23–27 read. The output pair rank inequality printed in the source reverses the input convention. Diagnostics adopt rank-decreasing pairs, consistent with the stated pides, and do not require the image to have pides 2^b1^a unless Phi-fixed.
339514.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Authors checked at most 10 rows. Corrected script switch2.py exhausts all placement words of object length 1–10 for coprime input row count (at most 20); switch_sample.py samples 10000 words at each object length 12,16,24,32,64,100 (rows up to 200). No dinv mismatch under that convention. Exact per-row accepted inputs in logs. Initial switch.py incorrectly filtered output pides and its mismatches are invalidated, not counterexamples.
339514.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Need source-faithful Phi implementation, fixed-point preservation, full noncoprime part (a), and an all-size argument or genuine witness. No full conjecture endpoint.

340195.title: The balanced cyclic composition proportion conjecture
340195.statement:
Let $C_n(132,213)$ denote the number of cyclic compositions of $n$ avoiding the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $C^B_n(132,213)$ denote the number of balanced cyclic compositions of $n$ (equivalently, balanced reverse layered permutations of length $n$) avoiding these patterns. Here $\frac{C^B_n(132,213)}{C_n(132,213)}$ is considered along the even positive integers $n$.

**Balanced cyclic composition proportion conjecture.** For even $n$,

$$
\frac{C^B_n(132,213)}{C_n(132,213)} = \Omega(1).
$$

The conjecture asserts that balanced cyclic compositions comprise a nonvanishing proportion of all $(132,213)$-avoiding cyclic compositions as the even size grows. The source presents this as a conjecture suggested by computer data, and no resolution is supplied.
340195.review_depth: Definitions 1.3, §2.1–2.2, Theorem 1.4 and §5 Conjecture 5.1 read. Balanced means a prefix sum equals n/2; cyclic means the reverse-layered permutation is one cycle, not a composition modulo rotation.
340195.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Authors report even n through 74. more.py comp exhausts all 2^(n-1) compositions for even n=2..22; cyclic/balanced counts logged. At n=22: 5960 cyclic, 2182 balanced. This does not go beyond the source range. C++ acceleration could not run: no g++ installed; no dependency installed.
340195.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Need uniform lower bound for the balanced fraction or asymptotic decay. A finite low fraction cannot refute Omega(1). No asymptotic mechanism closed.

340354.title: Non-unicyclicity conjecture for even-degree compositions
340354.statement:
Let $n$ be the degree parameter, and let $\sigma=\sigma_{n-1}\cdots\sigma_0$ be the composition of the permutations associated with the construction. A permutation is **unicyclic** if it consists of a single cycle on its underlying set. **Even-degree non-unicyclicity conjecture.** If $n$ is even, then

$$
\sigma=\sigma_{n-1}\cdots\sigma_0
$$

is not unicyclic. This was verified exhaustively for even $n\leq 30$, but the general assertion remains open.
340354.review_depth: Source §2.1 construction and Theorem 2/cycle discussion plus Conjecture 1 read. Rounds are x -> (x+b)^(-2^k) in a field of order 2^n.
340354.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: finite.py gf exhausts all irreducible binary polynomials and all perturbations for n=2,4,6,8: respectively 4,48,576,7680 cases; no single cycles. Authors claim checks through even degree 30.
340354.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: For n>=4 inversion has 2^(n-1)-1 transpositions, hence odd sign. Translation is even. Every invertible linear map on F2^n is even for n>=3 (elementary transvections each swap 2^(n-2) pairs), hence Frobenius powers are even. Each round is odd and an even number of rounds is even; a full 2^n-cycle is odd. n=2 is a direct four-point check. This classical sign argument is a routine bridge, not proposed significant credit; no Lean investment.

340430.title: Exponential-growth conjecture for Möbius values of the permutations $\kappa_n$
340430.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\kappa_n\in {\mathcal S}_{4n}$ be the permutation

$$
\kappa_n=n+1,n+3,\dots,3n-1,1,3n+1,2,3n+2,\dots,n,4n,n+2,n+4,\dots,3n.
$$

It is $321$-free and can be split into four quadrants, each an increasing subsequence of length $n$. **Exponential-growth conjecture.** The absolute value of its Möbius function satisfies

$$
|\mu(1,\kappa_n)|=\exp(\Theta(n)).
$$

Here “exponential in $n$” is recorded as exponential growth; the paper presents this as a conjecture motivated by computational experiments, and no resolution is supplied.
340430.review_depth: Literal kappa_n, primary §4 Conjecture 4.1, comparison with pi_n and chain-count upper bounds read.
340430.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: more.py mobius computes exact principal Mobius values by all distinct standardized subpatterns for n=1..4: -1,-27,-117,-509. The largest case caches 5165 patterns. These finite data cannot decide exp(Theta(n)).
340430.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Need a recurrence or sign-controlled embedding cancellation for all n; finite nonzero values do not prove exponential growth. A thesis lead with values through kappa_7 was found but its body was not fetched/read.

347533.title: Regularity conjecture for even associated lattices
347533.statement: Let $a>2$ be even and let $b$ be sufficiently large. Consider an Ulam set with generators $v_1$ and $v_2$ whose associated lattice is generated by $(-a,b)$. **Regularity conjecture.** The Ulam set contains finitely many elements of the form $2xv_1+yv_2$ and is therefore regular. The claim is based on computations and is presented as unresolved in the source.

Here v1=b, v2=a realizes lattice (-a,b); b is odd so generator-v1 parity is integer parity. Per-case total and last even element logged. This omits torsion lattice cases.
347533.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Finite apparent termination of even terms cannot prove eventual regularity. Need uniform no-new-even mechanism for sufficiently large b or an infinite exceptional family; no finite sweep can negate the unspecified threshold.

The formula is suggested by computations for $m=5,6,7$ and is not proved in the supplied text.

\phi_2(P)=1+\sqrt{7/3}.

374244.title: Cyclic Ramsey conjecture for complete graphs and alternating paths
374244.statement:
Let $K_a$ be a complete graph of order $a$ and $P_b^\mathrm{alt}$ an alternating path of order $b$. **Complete-graph cyclic conjecture.** For any $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, we have

$$
R_\mathrm{cyc}(K_a, P_b^\mathrm{alt}) = 1 + (a - 1)(b - 1).
$$

The claim is suggested by the computational data and contrasts with the proposed larger ordered Ramsey numbers. The cyclic equality remains open.

375364.title: The tropical chromatic number conjecture for Euclidean space
375364.statement:
Let $d4a3^n$ be equipped with the tropical metric, and let $d4a4^n$ denote its integer lattice with the induced tropical metric. The **tropical chromatic number conjecture.** The tropical chromatic numbers of both spaces are

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbb{Z}^{n})=\chi_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbb{R}^{n})=2^n.
$$

The conjecture is verified in dimensions $n\leq 3$; the general case remains open.
375364.review_depth: Primary tropical norm, Theorem 3.2 coloring construction, Conjecture 3.4, Theorem 5.1 and equilateral lower-bound discussion read.

375504.title: Stabilizing solution conjecture for the line-graph structural space
375504.statement:
Let $H$ be the stabilizing positive semidefinite solution of the reduced discrete algebraic Riccati equation under Assumption~, and let ${\mathcal V}_{\mathcal L}$ denote the structural subspace associated with the line graph. **Stabilizing solution conjecture.** Under Assumption~, the matrix $H$ belongs to ${\mathcal V}_{\mathcal L}$:

$$
H\in{\mathcal V}_{\mathcal L}.
$$

Exhaustive searches over all directed trees with at most six vertices found this property in every tested case. The conjecture proposes that the observed refinement ${\mathcal V}_{\mathcal L}$ contains the stabilizing solution generally, although the paper proves containment only in the weaker space ${\mathcal V}_{\mathcal B}$ and gives a counterexample showing that the corresponding invariance proposition cannot be extended to ${\mathcal V}_{\mathcal L}$.
375504.review_depth: Original v1 Conjecture 1, Assumption 1, reduced DARE and spaces read. Current source Theorem 2 statement and all five proof steps read, including weighted component lower bounds, simultaneous attainment, DARE/stability and intersection bridge.
375504.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: riccati.py enumerates unlabeled underlying trees and all edge orientations at orders 4..9, at beta=.5,.9: 32+96+384+1408+5888+24064=31872 numerical DARE cases, zero numerical solver failures, max span residual <3.6e-14. These extend v1 order 6 but are superseded by source full proof.
375504.remaining_lemmas_or_limits: Current Theorem 2 explicitly proves H in V_L for arbitrary oriented connected trees, with positive height-component formula. Therefore already source-resolved, zero credit; no Lean packet.
